assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Yūki across V01-V10 by game count and located state, in story order rather than disclosure order: #1 Maiden Race as an underinformed beginner who does not know the game is lethal (disclosed V06); #3 and Hakushi's offer (disclosed V05); #9 Candle Woods and the ninety-nine vow; #10 Scrap Building; #28 Ghost House; #30 and the lost left fingers; the eye thresholds (#61 loss of right light perception, #62 temporary left loss, #64 adapted perception, #65 fear); #70 and the decision to keep living parts; #73; #82 defeat by Kagura and the further injury; #86 leg failure; #90 wardrobe handover; #93 and its collapse; the open V10 hospital scene as endpoint. assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a located account of how the ninety-nine purpose becomes hers by use (borrowed from Hakushi's example, adopted under Kyara's pressure at #9, sustained by changed routines) and of mixed motives that do not collapse (利他 as practical self-interest beside real liking and leadership at #28). Not B: it states that affection, necessity and leadership do not reduce to one motive, that her lethal-allocation choices need the local rule and her believed alternatives, and that the post-#82 affective change has no exhaustive cause, so the evidence does not say which motive decides in her central decision class. Not D: the purpose, its maintenance and its limits are explained with located episodes in every volume.

States are located by game count and volume, with story order separated from disclosure order (#1 in V06, #3 in V05), and the bodily thresholds are causally traced: fingers at #30, the eye sequence #61-#65, the #70 choice to keep living parts, the #82 failure and later prosthetic and medical routine. Not A: the cause of the post-#82 affective change is left open and the endpoint is an unresolved hospital scene. Not C: the changes are explained, not just summarized, and each state carries its own evidence.

Written Japanese register is analyzed by audience: the reduced polite introduction 幽鬼っていいます and plain questions with newcomers at #28, 気に入った！ and imperatives to Mishiro, エージェントさん with formal thanks and ざっくりいっちゃってください to Setsuna, それは、言えないんです and くたばる with the landlady, また会ったね、藍里 and どう思う？ at #93, 悪いね alone. Not B: roughly a dozen short forms in a handful of relationships, no general politeness rule, and the monograph says ordinary pitch, accent and conversational recording are unavailable. Not D: the forms are tied to function and recipient, not listed.

Ordinary life is located and specific: room 107 at Tochinoki, indoor and outdoor tracksuits, delayed hygiene, night walks, the profile's ice cream and dislike of daytime, evening school with Ramona's English help, the retained lease, the hospital-adjacent routine of monitoring, medicine and prescribed food, the box handover. Not B: the monograph stresses that each detail comes from a different setting with a different range of application, and gives no account of what decides ordinary choices outside these scenes. Not D: the details are tied to state changes (before and after #9, after #82).

The monograph explains what changes her response with each partner: Hakushi's authority shifting from captor to chosen teacher to a living retiree she can disagree with; Setsuna's professional-intimate service with an asymmetry Yūki does not know; Airi's cooperation turning lethal under Jamboree assignment; respect for Maguma's specific strengths; declining Shiro's offer to avoid binding promises; Mishiro's group refusing her authority; privacy with civil acquaintances. Not A: Setsuna's reasons stay on her side, and Yūki gives no witnessed acknowledgment that mirrors Airi's attachment. Not C: the conditioning variables (authority, knowledge, assigned role, danger, disclosure risk) are explicit and attested across several partners.

Narration gives her stated reasoning in located moments: the #9 vow as an answer to Kyara, the three private minutes after #28, relief at losing to Kagura at #82, the comparison with Hakushi in the hospital, the inability to imagine after #99, and her tactical account of #93. Not B: her reason for accepting Hakushi's offer is left open, she misreads Setsuna's pause, and the post-#82 change in fear is described only from competing outside views and her own partial account. Not D: interior states are repeatedly located and kept separate from other characters' readings.

Tactical play is described as identifying the operative constraint, separating a stated rule from its physical world and trusting particular contributions (#28, Cloudy Beach, #93 ruling request); located lethal acts include the nearest-person rule at #28, the fatal order in Phantom Thief, the Kōen wager and disabling Airi at #93. Not B: the monograph limits the #28 rule to its example and says outcomes when only one beneficiary can meet a requirement need the local rule and her believed alternatives, so who she will harm or protect is not discriminated. Not D: the tactical method recurs across many games with located outcomes and failures.

Located positions are clear: she declines Keito's out-of-game killing, intervenes when someone is in live danger and help can be given (Ramona, Kōen, Sana), apologizes too late at #28 and keeps a private remembrance, and gives grief a permitted place after Snow Room. Not B: the monograph refuses a general ranking of whom she would save, and pairs collective protection with a fatal order in Phantom Thief, so no discriminating ethical policy is established. Not D: each position has a located episode and a stated rationale.

Only local items: the rough くたばる joke with the landlady, laughing at a spelling mistake at #93 inside a tactical display, and friendly inflection toward Airi in a lethal encounter. Not D: these are isolated moments with no analysis of humor as a pattern.

The monograph covers the whole admitted V01-V10 run, routes every material claim to spine and paragraph locators, tracks disclosure order separately from story order, preserves source contradictions (Hakushi's count of 96 against 95; the eye taken at #82) and states what lies outside (romance, post-V10). Not A: it is one literary portrait, with no curated operational model, ledger or validation on this subject, and the source run ends on an open scene. Not C: coverage is complete for the declared boundary.

Affirmative evidence of her limits and mistakes: acting at #28 before testing alternatives, failing to win authority in Scrap Building, #65 fear surviving her trained perception, misreading Setsuna's pause, missing Ramona's treatment connection, not asking who reached the rescue ship, and being unable to imagine life after #99. Not A: the evidence does not explain the post-#82 change in fear. Not C: the limits are located and stated as findings, not inferred from silence.

Game counts, volume, spine and paragraph locators place nearly every claim; the monograph warns that the profile age does not date #1 or #9 and separates what she knows at each point from what readers learn later. Not A: some states are given by period (before Candle Woods, after #82) rather than a located boundary. Not C: chronology splits are located inside volumes, for example the #70 choice and the #82 injury.

known_limits.statement: Whom she will kill, sacrifice or protect when a rule demands a victim is not discriminated: the #28 nearest-person rule is tied to one severe example, and the monograph says such outcomes need the local rule and the alternatives she believes she has.

The change in her access to fear after #82, visible at #93, has competing outside explanations (Maya, Airi, Busutake) and only a partial tactical account from her, with no established cause; pre-#82 composure and capability do not transfer to that state.

A model must use her knowledge, not the reader's: she does not know Setsuna helped at #1 and chose the assignment for that reason, she did not know #1 was lethal, and she learns Hakushi is alive only after Cloudy Beach.
Trained perception does not give universal composure: #65 still unsettles her after the adaptation shown at #64.

The source ends with her alive in hospital while the artisan and Busutake propose conflicting treatment; her choices, treatment and custody after that, and life after #99, are open, and she herself cannot imagine the day after #99.
Setsuna's reasons for her sedation choice, the new home and keeping the boxes belong to Setsuna; no joint decision about resting or continuing is established.
Only written Japanese register is available; pitch, accent and extended ordinary conversation are not evidenced.
No relationship history, partner preference, sexual identity or pattern of intimacy is evidenced.
The curated evidence is one literary monograph; no operational model, decision ledger or model check is curated on this subject, so the narrow conditional predictions rest on one line of evidence.
